quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Could you ___ me twenty pounds until Friday? I'll pay you back on payday.
quests.completeSentence: Could you lend me twenty pounds until Friday? I'll pay you back on payday.
quests.contextClue: The speaker promises to return the money later.
quests.hint: You hand something over now and expect to get it back.
quests.explanation: You lend something TO someone and borrow something FROM someone. Here the speaker is the one receiving, so the other person must lend.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'lend' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'lend' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Can you ___ me to call the bank tomorrow? I'll forget otherwise.
quests.completeSentence: Can you remind me to call the bank tomorrow? I'll forget otherwise.
quests.contextClue: Forgetting is the worry.
quests.hint: Help someone not to forget.
quests.explanation: 'Remind someone to do something' means help them remember. 'Remember' is what you do yourself: 'I remembered to call'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'remind' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'remind' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Could you speak up? With all this traffic noise I can't ___ a word you're saying.
quests.completeSentence: Could you speak up? With all this traffic noise I can't hear a word you're saying.
quests.contextClue: Traffic noise makes sounds hard to pick up.
quests.hint: Notice a sound with your ears.
quests.explanation: 'Hear' is about sound reaching your ears without effort, while 'listen' means paying attention on purpose.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'hear' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'hear' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: She ___ that she would call back, but she never did.
quests.completeSentence: She said that she would call back, but she never did.
quests.contextClue: No listener is named after the blank.
quests.hint: The past of the verb used to report words when no listener is named.
quests.explanation: 'Say' goes with the words spoken or a 'that' clause: 'She said that...'. 'Tell' needs a person: 'She told me that...'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'said' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'said' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Do you ___ any other languages besides English?
quests.completeSentence: Do you speak any other languages besides English?
quests.contextClue: The question is about languages.
quests.hint: Use a language to communicate.
quests.explanation: We 'speak' languages: 'speak Spanish'. 'Talk' is used for conversations: 'talk to someone'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'speak' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'speak' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: He ___ me a funny story about his first day at work.
quests.completeSentence: He told me a funny story about his first day at work.
quests.contextClue: 'Me' follows the blank, and a story is what was passed on.
quests.hint: The past tense of the verb used when you pass a story to a person.
quests.explanation: 'Tell' takes a person and something communicated: 'tell me a story', 'tell the truth'. 'Say' does not usually take a person directly.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'told' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'told' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I'm looking for a new ___; my current one is too far from home.
quests.completeSentence: I'm looking for a new job; my current one is too far from home.
quests.contextClue: 'A new ___' and 'my current one' show a countable position.
quests.hint: A specific paid position.
quests.explanation: A job is a specific paid position and is countable: 'a job', 'two jobs'. 'Work' is the general activity and is uncountable.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'job' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'job' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Our new flat is empty, so we need to buy some ___ before we move in.
quests.completeSentence: Our new flat is empty, so we need to buy some furniture before we move in.
quests.contextClue: An empty flat needs things to sit on and sleep on.
quests.hint: Tables, chairs, sofas and beds, thought of as a group.
quests.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable: 'some furniture', 'a piece of furniture', never 'furnitures'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'furniture' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'furniture' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: On the form, next to your name and address, there's a box for your ___.
quests.completeSentence: On the form, next to your name and address, there's a box for your occupation.
quests.contextClue: A form asks for personal details.
quests.hint: What a person does for a living, as written on official forms.
quests.explanation: 'Occupation' is the formal word for a person's job, used on forms and official documents.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'occupation' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'occupation' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I never ___ TV in the morning; I prefer to listen to the radio.
quests.completeSentence: I never watch TV in the morning; I prefer to listen to the radio.
quests.contextClue: TV is something looked at over time.
quests.hint: Look at something moving for some time.
quests.explanation: We 'watch' TV, a film or a match, meaning look at something for a period. 'See' is used for noticing.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'watch' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'watch' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I didn't ___ your haircut until Sarah mentioned it.
quests.completeSentence: I didn't notice your haircut until Sarah mentioned it.
quests.contextClue: Someone else had to point it out.
quests.hint: Become aware of something you see.
quests.explanation: 'Notice' means become aware of something: 'I didn't notice the sign'. It differs from 'look' or 'watch', which are deliberate.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'notice' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'notice' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Our team ___ the champions in the final by two goals.
quests.completeSentence: Our team beat the champions in the final by two goals.
quests.contextClue: The champions are the object of the sentence, so the verb is about defeating.
quests.hint: Defeat an opponent.
quests.explanation: 'Beat' takes the opponent as its object: 'beat the champions'. 'Win' takes the competition: 'win the final'. Beat is irregular: beat, beat, beaten.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'beat' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'beat' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: My uncle ___ me how to swim when I was six.
quests.completeSentence: My uncle taught me how to swim when I was six.
quests.contextClue: The uncle is the instructor, not the learner.
quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for giving someone lessons.
quests.explanation: 'Teach' is what the instructor does; 'learn' is what the student does. Teach is irregular: teach, taught, taught.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'taught' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'taught' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: That blue shirt really ___ you; the colour is perfect.
quests.completeSentence: That blue shirt really suits you; the colour is perfect.
quests.contextClue: 'The colour is perfect' concerns appearance, not size.
quests.hint: Looks good on a person.
quests.explanation: 'Suit' is about how something looks on you (colour, style), while 'fit' is about size.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'suits' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'suits' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: This key doesn't ___ the lock; are you sure it's the right one?
quests.completeSentence: This key doesn't fit the lock; are you sure it's the right one?
quests.contextClue: A key and a lock must match in shape.
quests.hint: Have the right size and shape to go into a space.
quests.explanation: 'Fit' is about size and shape: 'fit the lock', 'fit in a bag'. 'Suit' is about appearance.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'fit' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'fit' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Someone ___ my bike from outside the station last night.
quests.completeSentence: Someone stole my bike from outside the station last night.
quests.contextClue: The object is the bike, which is a thing.
quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for taking something that isn't yours.
quests.explanation: You 'steal' things and 'rob' places or people: 'stole my bike', 'robbed a bank'. Steal is irregular: steal, stole, stolen.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'stole' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'stole' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: A man with a mask ___ the bank on Main Street yesterday.
quests.completeSentence: A man with a mask robbed the bank on Main Street yesterday.
quests.contextClue: A masked man and a bank set the scene.
quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for taking things from a place or person by force.
quests.explanation: 'Rob' takes the place or person as its object: 'rob a bank', 'robbed a shop'. 'Steal' takes the stolen item.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'robbed' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'robbed' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Buying in bulk is more ___ than buying small packets.
quests.completeSentence: Buying in bulk is more economical than buying small packets.
quests.contextClue: Comparing bulk and small packets is about saving.
quests.hint: Saving money or resources.
quests.explanation: 'Economical' means saving money or resources, while 'economic' relates to the economy: 'economic growth'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'economical' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'economical' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: My skin is very ___, so I can't use strong soaps.
quests.completeSentence: My skin is very sensitive, so I can't use strong soaps.
quests.contextClue: Strong soaps cause a reaction.
quests.hint: Easily affected or irritated by something.
quests.explanation: 'Sensitive' means easily affected: 'sensitive skin', 'sensitive to noise'. 'Sensible' means practical and reasonable.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'sensitive' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'sensitive' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: He lives ___ in a small cottage, but he says he never feels lonely.
quests.completeSentence: He lives alone in a small cottage, but he says he never feels lonely.
quests.contextClue: 'Never feels lonely' contrasts with being by himself.
quests.hint: Without other people.
quests.explanation: 'Alone' describes being physically by yourself; 'lonely' describes feeling sad about it. You can be alone without being lonely.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'alone' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'alone' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Today is a ___ day for our country; no woman has ever won this election before.
quests.completeSentence: Today is a historic day for our country; no woman has ever won this election before.
quests.contextClue: A first-ever result makes the day worth remembering.
quests.hint: Important enough to be remembered in history.
quests.explanation: 'Historic' describes something important in history, while 'historical' means related to the past: 'a historical novel'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'historic' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'historic' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Prices have ___ sharply over the past year.
quests.completeSentence: Prices have risen sharply over the past year.
quests.contextClue: Prices go up on their own, with no object after the verb.
quests.hint: The past participle of 'rise'.
quests.explanation: 'Rise' is irregular and has no object: rise, rose, risen. 'Raise' needs an object: 'raise prices'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'risen' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'risen' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: There's very ___ time left, so we need to hurry.
quests.completeSentence: There's very little time left, so we need to hurry.
quests.contextClue: 'Time' is uncountable.
quests.hint: Not much; used with something you can't count.
quests.explanation: Use 'little' with uncountable nouns (time, money) and 'few' with countable ones (people, chairs).
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'little' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'little' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: How ___ people are coming to the party? I need to know how much food to make.
quests.completeSentence: How many people are coming to the party? I need to know how much food to make.
quests.contextClue: 'People' can be counted.
quests.hint: A word that asks about a countable number.
quests.explanation: 'How many' asks about countable things; 'how much' asks about amounts you can't count.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'many' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'many' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: This pen doesn't work. Do you have ___?
quests.completeSentence: This pen doesn't work. Do you have another?
quests.contextClue: A broken pen needs a replacement.
quests.hint: One more of the same kind.
quests.explanation: 'Another' means one more or a different one. It combines 'an' and 'other': 'another pen'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'another' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'another' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I'd love to have my ___ flat instead of sharing with three people.
quests.completeSentence: I'd love to have my own flat instead of sharing with three people.
quests.contextClue: Sharing is contrasted with sole ownership.
quests.hint: Belonging to you and no one else.
quests.explanation: 'My own' emphasises that something belongs only to you: 'my own room', 'their own business'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'own' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'own' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Every student got a certificate, and ___ one was signed by the principal.
quests.completeSentence: Every student got a certificate, and each one was signed by the principal.
quests.contextClue: Individual certificates are being considered one by one.
quests.hint: Used to talk about members of a group one by one.
quests.explanation: 'Each' focuses on individual members, while 'every' treats them together. 'Each one' is a common phrase.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'each' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'each' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: How can we ___ making the same mistake next time?
quests.completeSentence: How can we avoid making the same mistake next time?
quests.contextClue: 'Next time' is about staying clear of an error.
quests.hint: Keep away from something.
quests.explanation: 'Avoid + -ing' means keep away from doing something: 'avoid making'. 'Prevent' needs a different pattern: 'prevent us from making'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'avoid' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'avoid' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: She gave me a lovely ___ on my presentation, which made my day.
quests.completeSentence: She gave me a lovely compliment on my presentation, which made my day.
quests.contextClue: A kind remark made the speaker happy.
quests.hint: A kind remark about someone.
quests.explanation: A 'compliment' is a kind remark. 'Complement' means something that completes another thing. They sound the same.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'compliment' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'compliment' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I need to buy some ___ for the office: pens, paper and envelopes.
quests.completeSentence: I need to buy some stationery for the office: pens, paper and envelopes.
quests.contextClue: The list names items sold together.
quests.hint: Pens, paper and other writing materials.
quests.explanation: 'Stationery' is writing materials. 'Stationary' means not moving. They sound the same.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'stationery' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'stationery' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.
